subject: Acme trial credits - proposed balance reclassification / credit memo
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@acme.dev>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Acme trial credits - accounting treatment?

Hi team,

Quick ask — Acme applied two promotional items to their Oct invoice (Invoice #20261031):
- $30,000 promotional trial credit (approved via our promo deck, attached)
- $5,000 ad-hoc extension stipend we granted while they finalize procurement

We issued those as invoice offsets on the customer billing portal yesterday per the CS request (you can see the adjusted balance on the attached PDF). Sales confirmed the credit in writing (promo approval email attached).

Requesting guidance from finance/billing: what’s the preferred accounting treatment here? Options I think we have:
1) Issue a formal credit memo for the combined $35k (affects AR, creates CM record)
2) Book a journal entry reclassification from revenue -> contra-revenue (for recognition reasons) and leave invoice untouched (less disruption to AR)
3) Do a ledger reclass and leave as invoice offset in our billing system (if that’s acceptable for audit)

My ask: which path minimizes revenue recognition issues and gives Acme the clean evidence they need for their internal auditors? They may request a credit memo number. If we need approvals, I’ve attached the promo approval and deal summary.

Attachments: acme_invoice_20261031.pdf, promo_approval_email.pdf, deal_summary_ACME_Q4.xlsx

Thanks — I can jump on a quick call if helpful.

— Tessa
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@acme.dev>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Acme trial credits - accounting treatment?

Thanks for the context, Tessa. Quick notes from finance perspective:

- If the customer expects an official artifact for their auditors, a credit memo (option #1) is the cleanest approach. It creates a traceable AR adjustment and matches procurement expectations.
- For revenue recognition we need to know whether the original revenue for the invoiced amount was already recognized. If it was recognized in full, a credit memo plus a reversing journal entry is standard. If not recognized (e.g., invoice sits in deferred revenue) we can reclassify without a CM, but we must document the promo approval.
- For internal G/L: please tag the request with GL code: 4320-PROMO (contra-revenue).

Action items for Sales/CS (Tessa):
1) Confirm whether Invoice #20261031 revenue has been posted to recognized revenue (yes/no).
2) Confirm Acme’s preference for a credit memo number vs. invoice offset. Jordan — will your team need a CM number to close their quarter?
3) Upload signed promo approval (if you have it) — our auditors will want the signature.

I’ll draft the CM once you confirm and will coordinate with billing (Marissa) to issue CM & post the required journal.

- Marcus
Sr. Financial Analyst, Revenue Operations
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@acme.dev>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 08:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Acme trial credits - accounting treatment?

Marcus — answer inline below.

> If the customer expects an official artifact for their auditors, a credit memo (option #1) is the cleanest approach.
Yes — Jordan asked for a formal document they can attach to their procurement file.

> please tag the request with GL code: 4320-PROMO (contra-revenue).
Will do.

> 1) Confirm whether Invoice #20261031 revenue has been posted to recognized revenue (yes/no).
We confirmed with engineering billing that the invoice posted on 2026-10-31 and was partially recognized on 2026-11-01 (subscription & usage revenue recognized). I don’t have the exact ledger entries but CS indicated revenue hit recognized revenue.

> 2) Confirm Acme’s preference for a credit memo number vs. invoice offset. Jordan — will your team need a CM number to close their quarter?
Jordan: they prefer a credit memo number to include in their internal ledger and for their auditor packet.

> 3) Upload signed promo approval (if you have it) — our auditors will want the signature.
Attached: promo_approval_signed.pdf (signed by legal on 2026-10-29).

So requested path: please issue a credit memo for $35,000, post CM against Invoice #20261031, and create reversing journal entries to correct recognized revenue. Tag GL 4320-PROMO and include deal id ACME-2026-Q4-1578 on the CM memo text.

Thanks — I’ll let Jordan know timeline expectations.

— Tessa
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@acme.dev>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Acme trial credits - accounting treatment?

All — thanks for the clarity and the signed approval. Billing will process a formal credit memo and the associated reversing journal entries. Plan below:

- Create Credit Memo CM-2026-045 for $35,000 referencing Invoice #20261031, deal ACME-2026-Q4-1578.
- Post CM against AR; create reversing journal entries to reduce recognized revenue and post contra-revenue to GL 4320-PROMO.
- Provide PDF of CM and GL posting screenshots to both Acme (Jordan) and internal auditors.
- Target issuance: Fri 2026-11-14 EOD. If audit needs quicker turnaround, we can accelerate.

Jordan — once CM is posted you’ll receive a copy and the portal will reflect the adjustment. Please confirm if there’s a specific internal reference you want us to include in the CM description beyond the deal id.

Rafael — I’ll need the final JE batch id for our records after you post. Marcus — please confirm any AR aging impacts we should flag for the month close.

Marissa Cole
Billing Manager, Redwood Inference
Attachments: (none)
